lines.text: Let's start with the most famous rule in physics: F equals m times a.
F is force, in newtons. m is mass, in kilograms. a is acceleration.
Our robot is sixty kilograms. In the code that's robot mass, still waiting for a real weigh-in.
To speed up at ten: sixty times ten, six hundred newtons, or one hundred fifty per wheel.
Now, grip. The most a tire can push is mu times N.
N is the normal force: how hard the floor pushes up, the tire's share of the weight.
Weight is mass times g, gravity's pull, nine point eight one. Sixty times nine point eight one, over four: one hundred forty-seven newtons.
Mu, a Greek letter like a u with a tail, is the grip number. For good tread on carpet, it's about one.
So one tire can push one hundred forty-seven newtons to move its fifteen kilograms: nine point eight one, about ten. That's traction accel, about one g.
Notice the mass canceled out. A heavier robot needs more push, but also grips harder.
